_comment: SecurityInsight's DEPLOY CONTRACT. Ships WITH the solution (operator decision 2026-08-07) so changing how SI deploys never requires editing ~30 per-customer manifests. The customer's local Sync-AutomateIT.json says WHETHER they take SI; the central promotion map says WHICH VERSION and which capabilities are approved for their ring; this file says HOW. Three owners, three files, no overlap.
_needsSchema_comment: FALSE, and verified rather than assumed: SI has no relational database anywhere -- no DbContext, no Migrations, no SqlConnection, no EntityFramework. There is nothing to migrate. The SQL/schema half of the platform update design is PIM's problem, not a shared one.
_sia_removed_comment: SIA IS FULLY REMOVED FROM THIS CONTRACT -- 2026-08-08, in two steps, both operator-directed: 'remove the web-frontend from being deployed' / 'it is NOT used anymore and will be replaced by new design', then 'remove container also'. BOTH removed capabilities were SI Analyzer, not SecurityInsight: 'web-frontend' rolled the SIA web UI (revision roll, MI grants, Easy Auth) and 'container' built and rolled the SIA container image -- both through the same deploy hook, analyzer-web/deploy/Deploy-SIAnalyzer.ps1, which is now referenced by nothing. SIA was never delivered: its hosted live-verify gate never ran, FEATURES.md lists none of it, and its single internal environment (cae-sia / ca-sia) is being decommissioned. WHY THIS MATTERS EVEN THOUGH NOTHING DEPLOYS IT TODAY: the current production sync engine (C:\AutomateIT\bootstrap\Sync-AutomateIT-Engine.ps1) never invokes a deploy hook at all -- verified 2026-08-08, it reads this file only for capabilities and minPlatformVersion -- but the v3 distribution/orchestration split (DOCS/REQUIREMENTS.md section 7) WILL act on declared capabilities, and would have deployed a retired app on customers' behalf. A contract that declares something nobody should run is worse than one that declares nothing. Do NOT re-add either; the replacement belongs to the new design, not to this file. Guarded by tests/pester/SI-SyncContractReport.Tests.ps1.
_capabilities_comment: What KINDS of change an SI update performs. SecurityInsight is now a SINGLE-CAPABILITY solution: a pure code roll. 'code' is required and cannot be blocked -- a block is refused and reported, so nobody can brick their own install by declining the only thing the solution is.

capabilities.name: code
capabilities.description: The PowerShell engines and their rule/report catalogs -- plain file copy. This IS SecurityInsight; without it there is no solution. The engines run from disk on their next scheduled execution, so there is nothing to build, roll or health-gate at deploy time.

_deploy_comment: NO DEPLOY HOOK. Removed 2026-08-08 with the SIA capabilities -- the hook existed only to build/roll/health-gate SIA. SI's update is a pure code roll: the sync copies files, the engines pick them up on their next scheduled run. If the new design gives SI a deploy step again, declare it here with its appliesTo capabilities -- and only capabilities that still exist.
_requires_comment: NO PROVISIONING PRECONDITIONS. Both entries here (ACR + Container Apps environment for 'container', plus an Entra app registration for 'web-frontend') existed solely for SIA and went with it. SecurityInsight itself needs no Azure resource provisioned before an update: it is files on disk plus the workspace/DCE/DCR the engines' own bootstrap establishes.
